claims.text: Chemical short-range order typically suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
The suppression of lattice thermal conductivity by SRO is caused by enhanced phonon scattering rather than ordering-induced phonon coherence.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy that can exhibit chemical SRO.
MoNbTaW can be represented in both a random solid-solution state and an SRO state while retaining the same composition.
The disordered MoNbTaW state has high configurational entropy.
The disordered alloy has low lattice thermal conductivity because of mass-disorder scattering.
Controlled thermal annealing or other processing routes can induce SRO without producing long-range precipitates.
A relatively strong equilibrium SRO state in MoNbTaW can exist at 800 K above the associated long-range-ordering transitions and within a single-phase homogeneous solid solution.
The relevant temperature window for observing the proposed SRO effect in RHEAs is typically 300–1000 K.
SRO produces B2-like or L12-like local motifs that create atomic-scale periodic potential variations distinct from a random alloy potential.
In the disordered state, phonons are scattered by mass variance and random strain fields.
SRO creates a periodic potential that can open phonon band gaps or increase Umklapp scattering at selected wavelengths.
A mismatch between the SRO correlation length and the dominant phonon mean free path enhances scattering and reduces both phonon mean free path and lattice thermal conductivity.
In MoNbTaW, SRO enhances edge-dislocation mobility but reduces the rate of double-kink nucleation associated with screw-dislocation motion.
The SRO state will have measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than the fully disordered state of the same alloy composition.
The magnitude of conductivity suppression depends on SRO strength and the phonon wavelength spectrum.
SRO-induced conductivity suppression is strongest at intermediate temperatures where phonon-phonon scattering is significant but not dominant.
At very high temperatures, thermal vibrations can wash out the SRO contribution to phonon scattering.
At very low temperatures, matching of SRO correlation length and phonon wavelength could permit coherent transmission and enhance conductivity.
The influence of SRO on dislocation mobility becomes attenuated as temperature increases.
